one_liner: Hosted e-commerce platform that lets merchants build, manage, and sell through online stores.
access_note: A free Shopify Partner account plus a free development store gives instant Admin API access for building and testing; only public app listing on the App Store requires review.
api_breadth_note: Admin API (REST legacy + GraphQL primary) covers products, orders, customers, inventory, fulfillment, discounts, checkout extensibility, and more.
existing_mcp_note: Shopify ships an official Shopify Dev MCP server (docs/schema search) and a per-store Storefront MCP server for agentic shopping.

evidence.note: REST Admin API reference confirming REST is now legacy alongside GraphQL.
Official docs for Shopify's Storefront MCP server.

researcher_notes: Two distinct official MCP surfaces exist: shopify-dev MCP and Storefront MCP — worth clarifying which one a use case needs.

one_liner: Open-source e-commerce plugin for WordPress that turns a WordPress site into an online store.
access_note: Free, self-hosted plugin; the store owner generates REST API consumer key/secret directly from wp-admin with no vendor approval step.
api_breadth_note: Full CRUD REST API (v3) covering products, orders, customers, coupons, refunds, reports, and webhooks.
existing_mcp_note: WooCommerce ships a native MCP integration (developer preview) built on the WordPress Abilities API/MCP Adapter, plus community servers.

evidence.note: Official WooCommerce dev docs describing the native MCP integration.
Authentication docs: API keys and Basic Auth over HTTPS.

researcher_notes: WooCommerce's own MCP is explicitly labeled 'developer preview' — implementation is actively shifting.

one_liner: Cloud SaaS e-commerce platform with REST and GraphQL APIs for store management and storefront/headless commerce.
access_note: A free 15-day trial store (no credit card) and free Partner Portal sandbox stores give self-serve API accounts immediately; continued production use requires a paid plan.
api_breadth_note: REST covers store-level resources and a separate GraphQL Admin API and GraphQL Storefront API cover overlapping and headless use cases.
existing_mcp_note: BigCommerce publishes an official Storefront MCP server for AI shopping agents and a Developer Platform MCP for coding agents.

evidence.note: Official authentication docs: OAuth-based API accounts, X-Auth-Token.
Official BigCommerce blog announcing Storefront MCP.

researcher_notes: Multiple overlapping BigCommerce MCP offerings — worth confirming which is actually maintained/current.

one_liner: Enterprise B2C/B2B commerce platform (SFCC) offering REST APIs (SCAPI, and legacy OCAPI) for storefront and back-office operations.
access_note: No self-serve signup; a trial sandbox requires contacting a Commerce Cloud account executive or partner manager, and On-Demand Sandboxes require purchasing sandbox credits as an existing customer/partner.
api_breadth_note: SCAPI is organized into multiple API families covering catalog, cart, orders, customers, pricing, and promotions.
existing_mcp_note: Third-party/community Commerce-Cloud-specific MCP servers exist; Salesforce also has a broader platform-wide Agentforce MCP program.
main_blocker: No free self-serve developer sandbox; obtaining any environment requires sales/partner engagement or existing paid customer entitlement.

evidence.note: Official docs explaining SCAPI as the OAuth2/OAS3-based successor to OCAPI.
Confirms trial sandboxes must be requested via an Account Executive or Partner Manager.

researcher_notes: The most enterprise-gated app in the set — genuinely no free/anonymous way to get API credentials.

one_liner: E-commerce platform available as free self-hosted Magento Open Source or as Adobe-hosted/licensed Adobe Commerce (Cloud/SaaS), with REST and GraphQL APIs.
access_note: Magento Open Source is a free download where the store admin self-generates integration tokens with no vendor approval; Adobe Commerce SaaS instead requires Adobe IMS OAuth2 tied to a paid license.
api_breadth_note: REST and GraphQL APIs cover catalog, orders, customers, cart/checkout, CMS, and admin operations.
existing_mcp_note: Several unofficial MCP servers exist; no MCP server published directly by Adobe was found.

evidence.note: Official REST API overview.
Official docs distinguishing OAuth1.0a, token auth, and IMS OAuth2.

researcher_notes: Free self-hosted Open Source vs paid Adobe-hosted SaaS have meaningfully different access models — worth clarifying which one is meant.

one_liner: Website builder with integrated e-commerce (Squarespace Commerce) exposing REST APIs for orders, inventory, products, and profiles.
access_note: A site owner can self-serve generate a single-site API key, but building a distributable OAuth integration requires submitting a registration form that Squarespace manually reviews.
api_breadth_note: Commerce APIs cover orders, inventory, products, and site profile data — narrower than Shopify/BigCommerce, no full storefront/checkout API for third parties.
existing_mcp_note: Squarespace runs an official remote MCP server, but currently only exposes domain-search/purchase-link tools, not the broader Commerce API.
main_blocker: OAuth app registration requires manual Squarespace review, and the official MCP server does not yet cover core commerce operations.

evidence.note: Official docs on API key vs OAuth2 access for Commerce APIs.
Official docs describing the manual registration/review process.

researcher_notes: Worth double-checking current scope of the official Squarespace MCP server (developers-preview subdomain, may expand).

one_liner: Cloud e-commerce platform (by Lightspeed) with a free store tier and a REST API for catalog, orders, and customers.
access_note: Ecwid has a free store plan, and developers self-register an app in the Developer Portal to get OAuth2 client credentials for testing without a sales gate.
api_breadth_note: REST API covers products, categories, orders, customers, discounts, and store profile/configuration.
existing_mcp_note: No MCP server built by Ecwid itself was found; multiple third-party MCP integrations exist via Zapier, viaSocket, Vinkius, and Apify.

evidence.note: Official REST API reference overview.
Official docs confirming OAuth2 with private and public access tokens.

researcher_notes: Could not directly confirm free-tier API rate limits.

one_liner: Creator commerce platform for selling digital products, memberships, and subscriptions, with a REST API for products, sales, and subscribers.
access_note: Any Gumroad account holder can generate a personal access token instantly from Advanced Settings, or register an OAuth app, with no manual approval required.
api_breadth_note: API surface is centered on products, sales, subscribers, offer codes, and resource subscriptions/webhooks — a small, creator-commerce-focused set.
existing_mcp_note: Multiple community MCP servers exist plus integrations via Composio, Pipedream, and Zapier; no MCP server published by Gumroad itself was found.

evidence.note: Describes the OAuth2 endpoints and access-token generation flow.
Example community MCP server using a simple access token.

researcher_notes: Could not fetch gumroad.com/api directly; auth model is well corroborated across independent sources.

one_liner: Amazon's API for sellers/vendors to manage orders, listings, inventory, pricing, reports, and FBA operations programmatically.
access_note: Developers must complete a developer profile, pass identity verification, and register/get approved for a specific application type; private apps additionally require an active Professional Seller/Vendor account.
api_breadth_note: Covers catalog, orders, inventory, pricing, reports, finances, fulfillment (FBA), and notifications across many API sections.
existing_mcp_note: Several unofficial MCP servers exist; no MCP server published by Amazon itself was found.
main_blocker: Mandatory developer identity verification plus per-application-type approval (and separate Restricted Data Token approval) gates programmatic access.

evidence.note: Official SP-API registration overview confirming the developer profile, identity verification, and approval workflow.
Official onboarding docs distinguishing private vs public/vendor app registration.

researcher_notes: The clearest 'gated_approval' case among the ten — confirms the assignment's hint that SP-API requires approval.

one_liner: All-in-one payments, checkout, and fulfillment platform for creators/high-ticket digital businesses (rebranded to 'Commas' in 2026), with a REST API for checkout sessions, subscriptions, customers, and webhooks.
access_note: Merchants appear able to self-generate API keys from their own account, but the primary developer docs are gated behind login and it is unverified whether API access requires a specific paid plan tier.
api_breadth_note: Public reference covers checkout sessions, webhooks, customers, subscriptions, and discount codes — a small, transactional/payments-focused surface.
existing_mcp_note: No MCP server (official or community) was found for fanbasis/Commas.
main_blocker: Detailed docs require an authenticated account login to view in full, and it's unconfirmed whether a free/trial merchant account is sufficient for a working API key.

evidence.note: Public API reference (redirects to commasdocs.com).
Primary developer docs portal, but requires login to view details.

researcher_notes: fanbasis.com now redirects/rebrands to 'Commas' — the smallest/least-documented API of the ten, as hinted; needs a human to log in and confirm plan-gating.
